threats.title: User and workload identity confusion
threats.description: An agent action is attributed to the wrong developer, team, or workload.

threats.title: Long-lived credential exposure
threats.description: Agents or tools obtain reusable credentials beyond the task boundary.

threats.title: Prompt-driven tool misuse
threats.description: Repository content or tool output induces an agent to invoke an unauthorized action.

threats.title: Source and dependency supply-chain compromise
threats.description: An agent introduces untrusted code, packages, or artifacts into a change.

threats.title: Execution boundary escape
threats.description: Agent-executed code crosses the declared workload or tenant isolation boundary.

threats.title: Unauthorized data egress
threats.description: Source, prompts, credentials, or generated artifacts leave approved destinations.

threats.title: Model policy or residency bypass
threats.description: A request reaches a model or region outside the approved catalog and routing policy.

threats.title: Unauthorized or unreviewed repository change
threats.description: An autonomous action bypasses required review, approval, or protected-branch policy.

threats.title: Incomplete decision and action evidence
threats.description: A material agent decision or action cannot be reconstructed for investigation.

threats.title: Unbounded model or runtime consumption
threats.description: Runaway tasks exhaust quota, budget, concurrency, or shared platform capacity.

controls.title: End-to-end actor and workload binding
controls.description: Bind every task and downstream action to immutable workforce and workload identities.

verification.method: Run positive and cross-tenant negative authorization tests and inspect audit linkage.
verification.evidence_type: signed test result and audit samples
verification.acceptance_criteria: All actions contain matching actor, tenant, team, task, and workload identity; cross-tenant tests are denied.

controls.title: Task-scoped short-lived credentials
controls.description: Issue credentials only after policy evaluation and expire them at task completion.

verification.method: Inspect issued credential scope and attempt reuse after task termination.
verification.acceptance_criteria: Credentials are least-privilege, absent from logs, and unusable after the declared task lifetime.

controls.title: Schema-aware tool policy boundary
controls.description: Authenticate, authorize, validate, and record every tool invocation.

verification.method: Replay adversarial tool requests across allowed, denied, and approval-required actions.
verification.acceptance_criteria: All unauthorized and malformed requests fail closed; approval-required actions cannot execute without an approval record.

controls.title: Approved package and artifact path
controls.description: Resolve dependencies only from approved registries with provenance and integrity checks.

verification.method: Attempt direct public-registry access and inject an unsigned dependency.
verification.acceptance_criteria: Public bypass is denied and every accepted dependency has approved origin, version, and integrity evidence.

controls.title: Verified runtime isolation
controls.description: Enforce the selected process, container, microVM, or tenant boundary for untrusted execution.

verification.method: Run escape, filesystem, metadata, process, and neighboring-workload isolation tests.
verification.acceptance_criteria: Tests demonstrate the declared boundary and no access to host, metadata, or another task.
verification.frequency: each runtime image or platform release

controls.title: Default-deny runtime egress
controls.description: Restrict model, tool, package, and enterprise traffic to approved destinations.

verification.method: Probe approved and unapproved DNS names, IPs, ports, and proxy bypass paths.
verification.evidence_type: network policy test and flow logs
verification.acceptance_criteria: Only approved destinations succeed and every decision is observable with task identity.

controls.title: Fail-closed model eligibility
controls.description: Resolve models through a versioned catalog that enforces provider, region, and data policy.

verification.method: Request ineligible providers, models, and regions through every routing and fallback path.
verification.acceptance_criteria: Every ineligible route is denied and every eligible route records catalog version and policy rationale.

controls.title: Protected merge and approval boundary
controls.description: Require GitLab review, protected branches, and risk-based approval for material changes.

verification.method: Attempt direct push, self-approval, approval bypass, and merge with failed CI.
verification.evidence_type: GitLab policy configuration and negative tests
verification.acceptance_criteria: Protected changes require independent approval and passing mandatory CI; bypass attempts are denied and audited.

controls.title: Replayable tamper-evident audit trail
controls.description: Record requirements, model/tool actions, policy decisions, and GitLab outcomes with stable correlation.

verification.method: Select sampled tasks and reconstruct actor, inputs, decisions, actions, code changes, CI, and merge outcome.
verification.evidence_type: replay report and immutable record hashes
verification.acceptance_criteria: At least 99 percent of sampled tasks replay end to end with no unexplained identity or event gaps.

controls.title: Hierarchical quota and budget enforcement
controls.description: Enforce tenant, team, agent, model, and runtime limits before capacity is consumed.

verification.method: Drive usage through warning, throttle, and hard budget thresholds under concurrency.
verification.acceptance_criteria: Usage is attributed correctly and hard limits prevent consumption beyond the configured tolerance.

best_practices.title: Separate control and execution trust boundaries
best_practices.rationale: Compromise of agent-executed code must not grant control-plane authority.
best_practices.implementation: Use separate identities, networks, credentials, and audit paths for orchestration and execution.

best_practices.title: Fail closed on unknown tools and schemas
best_practices.rationale: Unrecognized capabilities cannot be safely authorized from natural language intent.
best_practices.implementation: Require registry membership, versioned schemas, owner, policy, and explicit action class before invocation.

best_practices.title: Use task-scoped credentials
best_practices.rationale: Credential lifetime should not exceed the authorized task lifetime.
best_practices.implementation: Broker short-lived credentials after policy evaluation and revoke them on completion or cancellation.

best_practices.title: Make GitLab the transaction boundary
best_practices.rationale: Repository policy and independent review provide a durable control point for generated changes.
best_practices.implementation: Use protected branches, required CI, CODEOWNERS, approval rules, and bot identities with no direct merge authority.

best_practices.title: Default-deny execution egress
best_practices.rationale: Agent-executed code and retrieved content are not trusted to choose destinations.
best_practices.implementation: Route model, tool, source, and package traffic through identity-aware approved gateways.

best_practices.title: Pin catalog and routing decisions
best_practices.rationale: A reproducible recommendation requires the exact eligible model and policy release.
best_practices.implementation: Record model, provider, region, router rule, fallback reason, and catalog content hash per invocation.

best_practices.title: Preserve an end-to-end action replay
best_practices.rationale: Token logs alone cannot explain code, policy, CI, and approval outcomes.
best_practices.implementation: Correlate advisor revision, task, spans, GitLab objects, CI, approvals, cost, and production result.

best_practices.title: Budget by outcome-owning team
best_practices.rationale: Global limits hide runaway tenants and prevent accountable optimization.
best_practices.implementation: Apply team quotas for concurrency, models, runtime, and monthly cost with explicit override workflow.
